disposition_reason: Fermentation-stage intervention study (Ecuador, Quevedo) inoculating Rhizobium japonicum at 0, 3 and 5% into 2 kg micro-fermenter batches of Nacional and Trinitario cocoa; Table 16 reports Cd in the resulting dried beans for six variety x dose cells. Effect is small (Nacional 0.36 -> 0.34/0.35; Trinitario 0.36 -> 0.30/0.29 mg/kg) and no Cd-specific variance or significance test is reported.
disposition_locator: Abstract; Materials and Methods (Table 1 arrangement, 'Cadmium test'); Table 16 p. 11368-11369; Conclusions p. 11369

study.design: processing study (fermentation-stage completely randomized bifactorial experiment, 3 replications)
study.material_scope: fermented, sun-dried cocoa beans of Nacional and Trinitario varieties; cocoa paste made only for sensory analysis (Cd not reported for paste)
study.growing_origin_vs_market: Pods harvested by the authors (Universidad Tecnica Estatal de Quevedo, Los Rios, Ecuador); farm/site not stated. Not a market sample.
study.sampling_unit: 2 kg micro-fermenter cell (6 treatments x 3 replications = 18 cells, 36 kg fresh mass); Cd printed per treatment (6 values)
study.method: 1 g crushed dry beans, microwave wet digestion with nitric acid, filtration, graphite-furnace atomic absorption
study.basis: dried beans as analysed; no dry-weight normalisation stated
study.qa: no CRM, recovery, or blank information reported

findings.material: fermented, sun-dried cocoa beans ("dry cocoa beans" crushed for analysis)
findings.basis: dried beans as analysed (sun-dried 6 days; moisture stated as reduced 'from 8 to 6%'); no dry-matter correction stated
findings.censoring: positive printed value; no LOD/LOQ reported
findings.locator: Table 16 (pdf pp. 11368-11369), 'Interaction of cocoa varieties by Rhizobium japonicum induction on cadmium concentrations in cocoa'
findings.notes: Single printed value per treatment cell with no SD, n, or statistical test for Cd. Design was 3 replications per treatment (Methods), but the table does not say whether the value is a mean of replicates. Nacional and Trinitario untreated controls both 0.36 mg/kg.
findings.integrity_issue: Abstract states Cd reduced 'from 36 to 29 mg/kg (ppm)', 100x higher than Table 16 (0.36 -> 0.29 mg/kg); table value adopted. Table numbering also inconsistent (text cites Table 17, printed as Table 16).

controls.control: Rhizobium japonicum liquid inoculant added to fresh fermentative mass (3% = 60 mL or 5% = 100 mL per 2 kg), 4-day box fermentation then 6-day sun drying
controls.outcome: Trinitario: bean Cd 0.36 -> 0.30 mg/kg at 3% (-17%) and 0.36 -> 0.29 mg/kg at 5% (-19%). Nacional: 0.36 -> 0.34 mg/kg at 3% (-6%) and 0.36 -> 0.35 mg/kg at 5% (-3%). No SD, n per value, or significance test reported for Cd; no mechanism or mass balance shown.

regulatory.product: cited generically as limits for 'cocoa paste used for chocolate production'; no numeric limit printed in the paper
regulatory.status: cited as in force; no value given

contradictions_with_stored_summary: Stored summary lists matrices including cocoa-paste; the primary reports Cd only for dried beans (paste used for sensory only).
Stored summary does not mention that the paper prints no SD, n per value, or significance test for Cd, nor the Table 16 vs 'Table 17' numbering mismatch.
Stored summary otherwise matches Table 16 values and correctly flags the abstract's 36 -> 29 mg/kg unit slip.
unresolved: Whether Table 16 values are means of 3 replications or single composites is not stated.
Whether analysed beans were whole (with shell) or nibs is not explicit; Methods say 'dry cocoa beans were crushed'; shelling is described only for the paste-making step.
Growing farm/site and harvest dates are not reported.
The paper claims all treatments 'comply with' EU 488/2014, but that regulation sets limits for chocolate/cocoa powder products, not beans; the compliance claim cannot be verified from the paper.
